claim_summary: Proposes a hierarchical multi-agent Agentic RAG in which a ReAct master agent routes each request to a task-specialized sub-agent built on instruction-tuned, DPO-aligned SLMs with retrieval-conditioned prompt pools, evaluated on forecasting, imputation, classification and anomaly detection.

claim_evidence.quote: Our Agentic RAG framework presents a hierarchical, multi-agent architecture composed of a master (top-level) agent and specialized sub-agents customized
In summary, the master agent orchestrates sub-agents, selects the most appropriate sub-agent, and allocates the task to the specialized sub-agent.

modules.name: ReAct master-agent routing
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK no: the router selects a sub-agent but embeds no task output requirement or validator; adding a task family adds a sub-agent to the action space without redesigning the router. R3_2_GTS no: no temporal semantics at router level. R3_3_GH yes: delegation and execution control. Sub-agents are invoked as tools in the ReAct loop, hence Tools and Execution.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:no - routing only, no task objective or validator
R3_2_GTS:no - no temporal semantics at router level

evidence.quote: In summary, the master agent orchestrates sub-agents, selects the most appropriate sub-agent, and allocates the task to the specialized sub-agent.

modules.name: Task-specialized sub-agents
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK yes: each sub-agent's objective, training data and output (forecast, imputation, cluster label, anomaly score) is fixed to one task family. Counterfactual holds: changing the task family requires a different fine-tuned SLM, prompt pool and output procedure.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - per-task objective and output; counterfactual holds

evidence.quote: It comprises a master agent that coordinates specialized sub-agents, each dedicated to a specific time series task such as forecasting, anomaly detection, or imputation.
However, in this work, the sub-agents operate in isolation, each handling only a single, specific task.
We evaluated the Agentic-RAG framework using a single, universal sub-agent for all tasks versus specialized subagents for each task.

modules.name: Task-specific instruction tuning of SLMs (PEFT)
modules.scope_reason: R2 LLM: QLoRA/PEFT updates SLM parameters on task datasets. R6: supervision shaping analytical outputs, so instruction_reasoning. Scope is instruction tuning only; DPO is split out.

evidence.quote: We fine-tune each SLM using instruction-tuning on task-specific datasets and optimize them for time series tasks such as forecasting,

modules.name: DPO alignment with dynamic masking
modules.scope_reason: R2 LLM: preference optimization updates SLM parameters; the masked binary classification supplies the preference signal. R6: aligns analytical outputs, so instruction_reasoning. Ablated separately (W/O DPO) in the paper.

evidence.quote: Additionally, we fine-tune using DPO[8] through a dynamic masking technique to align the SLMs task-specific outputs to preferred and non-preferred outcomes, providing adversarial feedback[47] through a binary classification task.

modules.name: Differentiable temporal prompt-pool conditioning
modules.scope_reason: R2 LLM: retrieved prompt values are concatenated to the model input embedding and projected by a learnable matrix, changing how the model receives the temporal input; the pool is described as differentiable. The paper also calls it a retrieval knowledge base, so a Harness memory reading (GTS context_memory) is possible; kept as LLM per the R2 boundary (parameter-updating), low confidence.
rubric_path: R2:LLM - alters model input representation with learnable projection

notes: Role fixed_workflow: the ReAct master can chain sub-agents, but the paper says that in this work they operate in isolation on one task each (L117-118), and no evaluated case shows returned feedback changing later actions. The paper's 'agentic' framing does not by itself meet the feedback-driven definition, so a human should confirm. Prompt pool: LLM placement follows the R2 boundary (learnable projection into the model input); the Harness memory reading is the main alternative. Excluded: SelfExtend long-context attention from [19] (used, not contributed; L325-326, L373); anomaly threshold from validation moving average (Eq. 1, L259-262); k-means regime labels for classification (L1384-1389); missing-data simulation (A.1); ablation tables are evidence, not modules. The sliding window is standard. Process validity and decision utility are not reported. Packet tables are text-extracted, so no numeric table values are quoted.
